questions.note: Order now right: in plan and V4o toe 2 ends about 5 mm behind the hallux, toe 3 about 15, toe 4 about 28, toe 5 about 47 (read at about 6 px/mm). The toes still don't read real: from above, 2-4 are slender fingers with bead knuckles, waisted shafts and dark clefts. From below they are ringed matchsticks. The 5th sits upright beside the 4th, nail forward, not rolled under.

Heights are right: in V8, with the heel's nearer floor corrected, lateral apex about 75 and medial about 88. The anterior crease now sits at z 80-85 (V1f, V2o). But the medial malleolus barely breaks the silhouette from behind. The lateral is a long soft swelling with no tip. The Achilles shows only as a faint ridge, and the side profile has no waist above the heel.

defects.what: From behind the heel is still a rounded box: near-vertical sides for about 30 mm (no visible taper between z 20 and z 45), a broad flat back face and a flat base. Only the corners are softer than before.
defects.fix: A heel from behind is a bell: widest in the pad near z 15-20, its sides converging in one continuous curve to the Achilles insertion, the back face domed over the tuberosity.

defects.what: The sole is a blank, even slab from heel to ball: no domed heel pad with its front margin, no lateral weight-bearing band, no medial arch hollow, no ball pad, only two faint transverse lines.
defects.fix: Model the plantar topography: heel pad dome, the lateral band rising into the medial arch hollow, a full ball pad across the MT heads with the sesamoid fullness under the 1st, then the toe sulcus.

defects.what: From below, toes 2-5 are thin stalks ringed by circumferential bands and ending in ball tips, separated by black gaps right down to the sulcus.
defects.fix: Plantar toes are plump, flattened pulps pressed side by side, each with a soft crease at the joints (not a ring), and a deep sulcus behind them.

defects.what: In plan, toes 2-4 read as fingers: long, slender, bead knuckles at the PIP, waisted shafts behind them, dark clefts between all of them to the webs.
defects.fix: A boot-wearing man's lesser toes are short and fleshy, broadest at the web, touching their neighbours, the PIP a low rise not a bead.

defects.what: The 1st MT head is a small round knob jutting from the medial border with a notch in front of it (also V5f): a bunion, not the broad low swell of the ball.
defects.fix: Spread the medial eminence into a radius-14 swell that blends into the hallux's base without a neck.

defects.what: The 5th toe stands upright beside the 4th with its nail facing forward like the others, a smaller copy of the 4th.
defects.fix: Rotate the 5th toe 30-45 degrees onto its lateral side, curl it, and tuck its tip under the 4th so its nail faces outward and up.

defects.what: From behind the medial malleolus barely breaks the silhouette: a faint shoulder where a broad round bony dome should stand out higher than the lateral.
defects.fix: A 30 mm dome about 5 mm proud of the shin line, apex z 89, clearly visible from behind and front.

defects.what: The lateral malleolus is a broad soft mound; its underside reads as a blurred round dark pit rather than a pointed fibular tip with a crisp hollow under and in front of it (same in V8: a long swelling, no tip).
defects.fix: Narrow the dome to about 24 mm with a defined, lower, posterior tip; the peroneal hollow below it a shallow groove curving forward, not a round crater.

defects.what: The heel still looks stuck on: a crease and notch where its upper lateral shoulder meets the lateral malleolus (also visible in V1f).
defects.fix: Run the heel's lateral side up into the peroneal groove behind and below the malleolus as one continuous surface.

defects.what: In side silhouette the back of the leg runs straight down and then leans back in one diagonal from about z 100 to the pternion: no concave Achilles waist, the heel reads as a boot's heel counter.
defects.fix: Keep the Achilles line nearly vertical to the insertion at z 52, with a small concavity there, and let the tuberosity bulge behind it only below that.

defects.what: Where the navicular tuberosity should be (about 120 mm ahead of the heel, z 42), the medial midfoot shows a small round dark dent in an otherwise flat wall; the arch hardly reads.
defects.fix: A 12 mm dome 2 mm proud at the navicular, with the abductor hallucis filling a long smooth vault below it.

defects.what: A thin dashed vertical seam line still runs down below the medial malleolus.
defects.fix: Remove the seam; the skin there is continuous.

defects.what: A Y-shaped pinch crease remains on the lateral sole, a mesh artefact with no anatomical cause.
defects.fix: Smooth it out; the lateral plantar band is an even, slightly convex surface.

defects.what: From the lateral side the toe tips are crimped and crumpled, and the 5th toe is a notched nub, like wrinkled plastic.
defects.fix: Each toe ends in a smooth rounded pulp; the 5th shows its lateral side, curled, with a soft dorsal knuckle.

defects.what: The extensor tendons on the forefoot are thin, evenly spaced, sharp-edged strings, the crispest relief on the foot, so the dorsum reads engraved.
defects.fix: EDL slips 3.5 wide and about 1 mm proud with soft shoulders, fading into the domed dorsum and diverging toward the toes.

defects.what: The hallux IP crease is still a single hard ring-step around the toe.
defects.fix: Two or three soft dorsal wrinkles over the joint, fading at the sides, no step.

defects.what: The 5th MT styloid is still a round marble under the skin on the lateral border.
defects.fix: A low elongated tuberosity, about 8 mm long and 2.5 mm proud, flowing into the lateral border.

defects.what: The front of the ankle has a crease now but no tibialis anterior cord: the tendons start on the forefoot and vanish before the ankle.
defects.fix: A 9 mm cord 1.5 mm proud running medial of the crease from the shin to the medial cuneiform, the strongest landmark at the front of a lean ankle.

defects.what: A wide dark slot, about 7 mm, separates the hallux from toe 2 along the hallux's whole proximal phalanx (also V1f), so the hallux reads as a separate thumb.
defects.fix: In a boot-wearing man the hallux lies against toe 2, touching or nearly so from the web to the tips.

defects.what: The lateral side meets the sole along a crisp, constant-radius edge from heel to ball (also the medial side in V2), like a shoe last's featherline.
defects.fix: The sides roll into the sole with a soft, varying radius: tight under the heel pad and ball, broad and low along the lateral midfoot.

ranked: [D2] The plantar view is still a mannequin's: one smooth slab with no heel pad, lateral band, arch hollow or ball pad. A podiatrist reads the sole topography first and finds nothing.
[D4] From above, toes 2-4 are fingers: slender, bead-knuckled, waisted and set apart by dark clefts. Real toes are short, fleshy and pressed together.
[D3] From below the lesser toes are ringed matchsticks with ball tips and black gaps between them.
[D1] The heel from behind is still a rounded box with vertical sides and a flat back. A real heel is bell-shaped, narrowing in one curve to the Achilles.
[D10] In profile there is no Achilles waist. The back of the leg leans into the heel from z 100 like a heel counter instead of standing nearly vertical down to the insertion at z 52.
[D7] The medial malleolus all but disappears from behind, so the ankle reads one-sided.
[D8] The lateral malleolus is a soft mound with a blurred round pit under it, not a pointed, lower fibular tip with a groove beneath.
[D11] The medial midfoot is a flat wall with a dent where the navicular tuberosity should stand, and the arch hardly reads in the medial view.
[D19] The hallux stands apart from toe 2 with a 7 mm slot along its whole base, like a thumb. In a boot wearer they lie together.
[D5] The 1st MT head is a bunion-like knob with a neck in front of it, not the broad low swell of the ball.
[D9] The heel looks stuck on: a crease and notch where it meets the lateral malleolus, instead of one surface running through the peroneal groove.
[D6] The 5th toe is an upright small copy of the 4th with its nail forward, not rolled onto its side and tucked under.
The ankle from z 100 to 200 is a parallel-sided column in V2 and V3. A lean man's ankle narrows above the malleoli, with the Achilles standing off the tibia over a visible hollow.
[D18] There is no tibialis anterior cord at the front of the ankle, so the new crease sits on a featureless surface.
Detail is uneven. The dorsal forefoot is busy with sharp relief while the heel, sole and hindfoot sides are bare, so the foot reads like a carved forefoot on a last.
[D14] From the side the toe tips are crimped and crumpled, and the 5th is a notched nub.
[D20] The sides meet the sole along a crisp featherline edge from heel to ball, a last's construction line rather than skin rolling under weight.
[D15] The extensor tendons are thin, sharp, evenly spaced strings, the crispest relief on the foot, so the dorsum looks engraved.
[D17] The styloid is still a round marble on the lateral border.
[D16] The hallux IP crease is a hard ring-step instead of a few soft wrinkles.
[D12] A dashed seam line runs below the medial malleolus in V2.
[D13] A Y-shaped pinch crease on the lateral sole in V4.
